title: Out of 100
goal: I can find a percentage of an amount from 10%, 5% and 1%. I can find a discount and GST, and avoid percentage traps.

learn.intro: Percent means out of 100. Build other percentages from 10%, 5% and 1%. A discount comes off the first cost. GST is charged on the cost after the discount.

example.problem: A bag costs $60. It has 30% off. GST of 9% is charged on the cost after the discount. How much does Ali pay?
steps: The cost after the discount is $60 - $18 = $42.

howto.title: How to
steps: Find 10%. Build the percentage you need.
Find the GST on the new amount.

try.text: A jacket costs $75. It has 20% off. GST of 9% is charged on the reduced cost. How much does Mei pay? $ {b}
try.explanation: 10% of $75 = $7.50, so 20% = $15 off. The cost after the discount is $60. 1% of $60 = $0.60, so 9% = $5.40. Mei pays $60 + $5.40 = $65.40.

items.text: The grid has 100 small squares. Some squares are shaded.
items.explanation: (a) 38 of the 100 squares are shaded, so 38%. (b) 100 - 38 = 62 squares are not shaded, so 62%.

items.text: Find each amount. Use 10%, 5% and 1%.
Write each as a percentage.

parts.label: a
parts.text: 18 out of 25 pupils wear glasses. That is {b}%.

parts.label: b
parts.text: 7 out of 20 pupils cycle. That is {b}%.

items.text: A bag costs $120. It has 15% off.
A watch costs $64 before GST. GST is 9% of the cost before GST.
Ravi has $150. He spends 20% of his money on a game. Then he spends 40% of the money that is left on a book. How much money does Ravi have now? $ {b}
There are 40 children in a group. 35% walk to school. 25% cycle. The rest take the bus.
Mei scored 21 out of 30 in Quiz 1 and 34 out of 50 in Quiz 2.
T-shirts cost $20 each. Shop P says buy 2 and get 1 free. Shop Q says 30% off each T-shirt. Siti needs 3 T-shirts.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The cheaper shop is   {circ:Shop P|Shop Q}

items.explanation: (a) She pays for 2 T-shirts: 2 × $20 = $40. (b) 30% of $20 = $6 off each, so $14 each. 3 × $14 = $42. (c) $40 is less than $42, so Shop P.

items.text: A shirt costs $50. The cost goes up by 20%. Then the new cost goes down by 20%.

parts.label: a
parts.text: After going up, the shirt costs $ {b}

items.explanation: (a) 20% of $50 = $10, so $60. (b) 20% of $60 = $12, so $60 - $12 = $48. (c) No. The second 20% is taken from $60, not from $50, so the cost does not come back to $50.

items.text: Each bar is cut into equal parts. Write the percentage that is shaded.
items.explanation: (a) 2 out of 5 equal parts: 2/5 = 40/100 = 40%. (b) 3 out of 4 equal parts: 3/4 = 75%.

items.text: Circle True or False.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A 20% discount and then a 10% discount is the same as a 30% discount.   {circ:True|False}

items.explanation: (a) 50% is a half: 40. (b) 90 ÷ 10 = 9. (c) False. Test with $100: 20% off gives $80. Then 10% of $80 is $8 off, so $72. A 30% discount gives $70.

items.text: Aisha has $200. She spends 40% of it on shoes. She spends 25% of the rest on a gift. How much money does she have left? $ {b}
items.explanation: 40% of $200 = $80 for shoes, so $120 is left. 25% of $120 = $30 for the gift. $120 - $30 = $90.

items.text: Ali pays 9% GST on a $250 sofa. Then he pays $20 to have it delivered. The delivery has no GST. How much does he pay in all? $ {b}
A $200 coat has 10% off. Then there is a further 20% off the new cost.
items.hint: Take the 20% off the new cost, not off $200.
items.explanation: (a) 10% of $200 = $20, so the new cost is $180. 20% of $180 = $36, so the coat costs $180 - $36 = $144. (b) The total discount is $200 - $144 = $56. $56 out of $200 = 28 out of 100 = 28%. It is not 30%.

items.text: After a 20% discount, a bag costs $60. What was the cost before the discount? $ {b}
items.hint: $60 is 80% of the old cost. What is 10% of the old cost?
items.explanation: The bag now costs 80% of the old cost. 80% is $60, so 10% is $60 ÷ 8 = $7.50. The old cost is 100% = 10 × $7.50 = $75. (Adding 20% of $60 would give $72, which is wrong.)

items.text: A table costs $218 with GST. GST is 9% of the cost before GST. How much GST is in $218? $ {b}
items.hint: $218 is 109% of the cost before GST. What is 1%?
items.explanation: The cost before GST is 100%. With GST it is 109%. 109% is $218, so 1% is $218 ÷ 109 = $2. The GST is 9 × $2 = $18. (9% of $218 would be $19.62, which is wrong because GST is 9% of the cost BEFORE GST.)

items.text: A cost goes up from $20 to $50, and then it goes back down from $50 to $20. The change is always compared with the amount you start from.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The percentage increase from $20 to $50 is {b}%.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The percentage decrease from $50 to $20 is {b}%.

items.hint: Increase = change out of the starting amount. Which is the start?
items.explanation: (a) The change is $30. Out of the starting amount $20: 30/20 = 150/100 = 150%. (b) The change is $30 again. Out of the starting amount $50: 30/50 = 60/100 = 60%. The same $30 change gives different percentages because the starting amounts are different.

items.text: In a group of 40 children, 40% are boys. 25% of the boys and 50% of the girls wear glasses. What percentage of the whole group wears glasses? {b}%
items.hint: Find the number of boys and girls first. Then count glasses.
items.explanation: Boys: 40% of 40 = 16. Girls: 24. Glasses: 25% of 16 = 4 boys and 50% of 24 = 12 girls. That is 16 children out of 40. 16/40 = 40/100 = 40%.

items.text: A jar has 50 beads. 60% of the beads are blue. The rest are red. Blue beads are added to the jar, and no red beads are taken out. Now 80% of the beads are blue. How many blue beads were added? {b}
items.hint: The red beads stay the same. Find their share of the new total.
items.explanation: Red beads: 40% of 50 = 20, and they do not change. After adding blue beads, red is 20% of all the beads. So 20 beads are 20%, and 100% is 100 beads. Blue now: 80. Blue at first: 30. Added: 80 - 30 = 50.

items.text: Find the amounts.
A book costs $40. It has 25% off. GST of 9% is charged on the reduced cost. Find the total cost. $ {b}
Kumar has $80. He spends 25% of it on lunch. He spends 50% of the rest on a gift. How much does he have left? $ {b}
items.explanation: 25% of $80 = $20, so $60 is left. 50% of $60 = $30 for the gift. $60 - $30 = $30 is left.

items.text: Test 1: 33 out of 50. Test 2: 16 out of 25. Circle the test with the higher percentage.   {circ:Test 1|Test 2}
items.explanation: 33 out of 50 = 66 out of 100 = 66%. 16 out of 25 = 64 out of 100 = 64%. 66% is higher, so Test 1.
